solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

Q052-01.notes: ax > 2a + 6; divide by a<0 and flip: x < 2 + 6/a. B is the no-flip trap; C/D are sign errors on 6/a. Distractors well-balanced.

Q052-02.notes: Need 3 - x <= x + k for some x <= -2, i.e. k >= 3 - 2x. 3 - 2x is minimized at x = -2 (value 7), so least k = 7 (boundary point (-2,5) satisfies all three). Graphing with slider also works but needs the setup insight.

flags: minor: accepted forms should include 17.5 and 35/2
Q052-04.notes: f(5) = 2f(5) -> f(5) = 0. Slope (0-7)/(5-3) = -7/2; f(0) = 7 + 3(7/2) = 17.5. Key insight (intersection forces f(5)=0) is non-obvious.

flags: minor: very standard compound-interest interpretation item, closely resembles common official/practice SAT items of this type
Q052-06.notes: Exponent 4t = number of compounding periods; 4 = compoundings per year. A describes 0.04 (nominal annual rate), C misstates 1% per period, B misreads.

Q052-07.notes: 0.5x + 10 + 200/x <= 35 -> x^2 - 50x + 400 <= 0 -> 10 <= x <= 40. Greatest 40 (C(40)=1400, avg 35). Graphing makes it routine.

flags: minor: answer-cue by plausibility - 0.14 and 2.8 min/mile are physically impossible running paces (world record ~3.7 min/mile), and 4.5 min/mile is elite-only, so a student with real-world sense can pick 7.2 without computing; key is also the largest value

Q052-09.notes: 0.6 in = 0.05 ft; 2000 * 0.05 = 100 ft^3/hr; *7.48 = 748 gal/hr. Inches-to-feet step is the trap. Magnitudes realistic.

Q052-10.notes: Sides 14cos30 = 7*sqrt3, 14sin30 = 7; area 49*sqrt3. A is the triangle-area (half) trap, C/D other slips.

Q052-11.notes: Triangle ACD right at D: 16 = (1/2)(4)(CD) -> CD = 8. Geometric mean: CD^2 = AD*DB -> DB = 16, AB = 20. Area = (1/2)(20)(8) = 80. Requires altitude-on-hypotenuse similarity insight.
